scope: CT tensor_group16 local-dynamic NVFP4 parts of the two locked target-model artifacts; BF16 inputs, original U8 low-first packed weights, E4M3FN group scales and original independent F32[1] WG/IG quantization multipliers.

activation.layout: Independently for each leading-index row and each consecutive group of 16 K elements. No per-token current global max is computed.
activation.global: IG is a stored F32[1] calibration parameter. dynamic=local initializes this global but does not store input_scale; only local scales are recomputed at forward.
steps: A is BF16. Group absmax remains BF16. u = BF16_RNE(amax / 6). This divide happens before the F32 global multiply.
v = F32_RNE(IG * F32(u)); IG has shape [1], promoting BF16 local scales to F32.
SF = E4M3FN_RNE(clamp(v,-448,448)), widened back to F32. Only exact SF==0 is replaced by 0.125. This is not max(SF,eps), min-normal, or the E4 min-subnormal.
effective = F32_RNE(SF / IG). Do not replace this division by SF * F32_RNE(1/IG).
FP4 pre-rounding is the real semantic difference: exact nightly casts this normalized value directly to E2M1; commit46196ce first rounds this clamped value to BF16, then E2M1.
E2M1 ties go to even magnitude code. Thresholds are .25->0, .75->1, 1.25->1, 1.75->2, 2.5->2, 3.5->4, 5->4.
QDQ = BF16_RNE(F32_RNE(F32(code_value) * effective)); the final group result is explicitly restored to original A dtype.

weight.ports: Wpacked U8[N,K/2], SF E4M3FN[N,K/16], raw WG F32[1]; A also needs raw IG F32[1]
weight.global_convention: CT raw WG/IG is a quantization multiplier, hence an effective-dequant divisor. ModelOpt's scaling_factor_2 is the dequant multiplier; these are not interchangeable input buffers.
steps: Unpack even K from low nibble, odd K from high nibble. Sign bit is 3; magnitude table is [0,.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,6]. Code8 is negative zero.
Canonical CT decompressor unpacks to BF16 by default, widens SF E4 to BF16 exactly, then computes F32_RNE(SF / rawWG).
Weight SF0 is directly decoded; unlike dynamic activation scale generation, weight decompression adds no epsilon or new validity guard.

Ordinary CT reference inference multiplies QDQ A and decoded W in their BF16 dtype. A future packed implementation must preserve the per-element BF16 operands, not substitute a code-dot with combined post-scales. The backend dot/reduction tree remains a separate contract.

version_difference.helpers: utils/helpers.py, lifecycle/forward_helpers.py, compressors/nvfp4/base.py are identical in the relevant retained versions (see version diff files).

version_difference.natural_schema: A numerical pre-rounding field (direct vs BF16) is sufficient to distinguish the finite normalized-value difference; do not encode model names, producer versions, or a routing whitelist.

witnesses.status: Pure Python scalar assertions passed; not a Hyle/producer numerical execution

signed_zero_and_nonfinite.A_negative_zero: Nightly and dev CPU use torch.sign, not a copied sign bit; exact signed-zero preservation is not explicitly guaranteed there. The dev Triton kernel explicitly carries the BF16 input sign bit, including -0.
signed_zero_and_nonfinite.negative_tiny_to_zero: For finite negative nonzero normalized values, thresholded +0 times sign=-1 produces -0 in the sign-multiply paths; Triton explicitly ORs the sign bit.
signed_zero_and_nonfinite.weight_code8: Unpack table's +0 multiplied by -1 yields -0; positive finite WG and finite nonnegative SF preserve the usual IEEE signed-zero path. No unsigned-zero reinterpretation is justified.
signed_zero_and_nonfinite.NaN: Nightly/CPU torch.sign+arithmetic and dev Triton comparison/bitwise-sign code are not one uniform NaN contract. In particular Triton NaN comparisons leave initial magnitude0; CPU arithmetic propagates a NaN. No actual backend special-value execution was performed.
signed_zero_and_nonfinite.positive_finite_globals: A sensible bounded consumer domain, but not proof all intermediates remain finite. F32 SF/global may overflow or underflow; 0*Inf can yield NaN. Preserve operation order and IEEE behavior rather than adding a new clamp/guard.
signed_zero_and_nonfinite.finite_overflow_tree: Local IG*u may overflow F32 and is then clamped by the E4 conversion; effective SF/IG can overflow even for positive finite IG. W SF/WG can similarly overflow; code0*Inf is NaN. Finite normalized A overflows are clipped to6 before FP4.

integration.shape: Two explicit FP4 pre-rounding policies under the existing prepared/native operation execution and resource lifetime machinery; dense and selected-grouped paths are both required. No runtime model/producer whitelist or new executor.
integration.chosen_portable_reference: Torch sign convention is explicit: a signed zero presented to the FP4 threshold stage maps to+0; a negative nonzero value which rounds to zero retains-0. The BF16 pre-rounding mode applies before that sign test. Original packed weight code8 retains-0.
integration.resource_gap: Checkpoint expert weights are separate tensors. Current grouped carrier requires one dense bank. Existing WeightSlots/catalog/selected fragments provide bounded uploading and lifetime building blocks, but the NVFP4 bridge for segmented experts, global/local ID mapping, working-set planning and real copy accounting is still to be completed under delivery3. Combining512 artifact18 role weights creates a4GiB W carrier and512MiB SF carrier, which is not a requirement of the checkpoint itself.

limits: No tensor payload values, publisher artifact execution, model import, quality or throughput were verified.

Artifact8 full header covers168 complete MLP NVFP4 roles in layers0-55; last8 layers MLP are FP8. Artifact18 only first of70 shards was inspected, covering1593 complete NVFP4 roles; additional global-only cross-shard entries are not complete roles.
A source-level independent scalar oracle is not execution of the original producer. Calibration observer/version and calibration payload are not reconstructed. Stored globals remain original ports.
Deployment FP4 tensor-core/code-dot paths, vLLM emulation variants and the producer fakequant tree are not assumed numerically equivalent.
This research archive makes no Hyle build, GPU, Linux, installed-consumer, complete bank or whole-model support claim. Hyle implementation and focused testing are in progress separately.
